intro: The education system, grants and marks, and what goes on in a student's head.

palabras.consejo: You «solicitas» it and it is «concedida» or «denegada». The one who gets it is «becario».
It gathers all the marks of your studies. You say «un buen expediente».
In life, «mi asignatura pendiente» is something important you have not done yet.
The opposite is «obligatorio». For the subject you say «una optativa».
It ends in an unstressed «-io»: «o-bli-ga-TO-ryo». The opposite is «optativo».
It comes from «presencia». The opposite is «a distancia» or «en línea».
You study «a distancia» from home, online or with materials sent to you.
It is the same in singular and plural: «una tesis», «dos tesis». It is feminine.
It comes from «sobresalir», to stand out. You «sacas» a sobresaliente.
You say «sacar un suspenso» or «suspender». The opposite is «aprobar».
It comes from «memoria». Memorising helps, but does not replace understanding.
It is irregular: «deduzco», «deduces». It is conjugated like «conducir» and «traducir».
It is an idiom: «me quedé en blanco» when the mind empties.
It takes «a»: «presentarse al examen». With «de» you say «examinarse de matemáticas».
«oral» is the same for masculine and feminine. The stress is on «RAL».
«tribunal» is masculine. In exams it means the panel of examiners.
«saber» means to know. The «ía» ending of the past is stressed on «BI»: sa-BI-as.

palabras.significado: to sit, to present yourself (infinitive with «te»)
palabras.consejo: «presentarte» = «presentar» + «te». In exams, «presentarse» means to sit the exam.
«convocatoria» is feminine: «la convocatoria». The «v» is pronounced «b».
«sacar un sobresaliente» means to get a top mark. «saco» is the first person of «sacar».
«pedir» means to ask for. The future accent falls on the last syllable: pe-di-RE.
«me presento a un examen» means I sit an exam. The stress falls on «SEN».
«examinarse de» is to take an exam in a subject. The «x» sounds «ks».
«matemáticas» is feminine plural. It always has the accent on «MA».
«facultad» is feminine: «la facultad». The stress is on the final «TAD».
«labio» is masculine: «el labio». The plural «labios» has the stress on «LA».
«fecha» is feminine: «la fecha». The «ch» sounds as in «church».
«escapar» means to escape. The «c» before «a» sounds «k»: es-KA-pan.
«asustado» means frightened. It agrees with «pájaros», masculine plural.
«profesor» is masculine: «el profesor». The plural adds «-es».
«museo» is masculine: «el museo». The «eo» is two syllables.
«deducir» means to work something out by reasoning. The «c» sounds «th».
With «se», «presentarse» means to sit an exam. The stress is on «TAR».
«aprobar» means to pass. The «ue» is a single sound: a-PRWE-ba.
«un notable» is a grade between seven and nine. It is masculine.
«quedarse en blanco» means to go blank. The accent marks the final stress: ke-DE.
«universitario» means related to university. The «v» sounds «b».
«mirando» is the gerund of «mirar». It is used for an action happening now.
«le» attaches to «hablar»: «hablarle» means to speak to someone.

texto:
**The stages.** Primary, secondary and sixth form; then **la universidad** or **la formación profesional**.

**Subjects.** They can be **obligatorias** or **optativas**. If you fail one, you have **una asignatura pendiente**. It is also said in life: «learning to swim is **mi asignatura pendiente**».

**Marks.** Out of ten: **suspenso** (below five), aprobado, notable and **sobresaliente** (nine or ten). All your marks make up **el expediente**.

**Exams.** **Presentarse a** an exam, aprobar, suspender, repetir curso.

**Money.** You apply for a **beca** and they grant it or deny it.

**Formats.** A course can be **presencial** or **a distancia**.

**In your head.** **Memorizar**, **deducir**, **sacar conclusiones** and, sometimes, **quedarse en blanco**.

**False friend.** **La carrera** is a university degree, not a running race.

Many verbs in the world of study take a fixed preposition. They should be learnt together:

- **Presentarse a** an exam: **me presento al examen**.
- **Examinarse de** a subject: **se examina de matemáticas**.
- **Licenciarse en** a degree: **se licenció en Derecho**.
- **Contar con** something: **cuento con una beca**.
- **Aprender a** + infinitive: **aprendió a mirar los cuadros**.
- **Dejar de** + infinitive: **dejó de repetir fechas**.

If you change the preposition, the sentence sounds wrong or changes meaning.

opciones.explicacion: Yes: deducir is reaching an idea from clues.
Memorizar is learning by heart; here you have to think.
Suspender is getting a bad mark in an exam.

opciones.explicacion: Presencial is the opposite: you have to be in the classroom.
Yes: «a distancia» is studying without being in the same place.
Optativo means it can be chosen, not where you study.
